content:
For years, collectors have been clamoring for Steve Jobs memorabilia, and a new item is sure to generate significant interest. This is his 8th-grade science fair project, which includes two demonstration circuits and a warning note Jobs gave to his teacher.

The item has been stored at the Jobs family property in Los Altos, but it is now one of over 200 lots in an Apple 50th anniversary auction...

Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and RR Auctions is holding a two-part auction to mark the occasion, called "Steve Jobs and the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction." The first part saw the sale of the first check ever written by the company, which went for an impressive $2.4 million.

The second part includes this science fair project.

The warning note likely reflects the risk that the circuits could burn out if left running too long. At the time of writing, online bids were under $3,000, but that is sure to change.

There is also a fully functional early Apple 1.

And an original iPod development prototype.
